source.text: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד מִנָּי֖וֹת בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֞א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ מֶֽה־עֲוֺנִ֤י וּמֶֽה־חַטָּאתִי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כִּ֥י מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled David from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? What [is] my iniquity, and what [is] my sin before your father, that [he is] seeking my life?

en.L: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and he came and said before Jonathan, "What have I done? What [is] my iniquity, and what [is] my sin before your father, that he [is] seeking my life?"
en.B: David escaped from Naioth in Ramah and went to Jonathan. "What have I done?" he asked. "What is my crime? What wrong have I done to your father, that he is trying to take my life?"
en.R: David ran away from Naioth in Ramah. He went to Jonathan and asked him, "What have I done? What crime am I guilty of? What wrong have I done to your father? Why is he trying to kill me?"

es.L: Y huyó David de Naiot en Ramá, y vino y dijo delante de Jonatán: «¿Qué he hecho? ¿Cuál [es] mi iniquidad, y cuál [es] mi pecado delante de tu padre, para que [él] busque mi vida?».
es.B: David escapó de Naiot, en Ramá, y fue a ver a Jonatán. «¿Qué he hecho?», le preguntó. «¿Cuál es mi delito? ¿Qué mal le he hecho a tu padre para que trate de quitarme la vida?».
es.R: David huyó de Naiot, en Ramá. Fue a ver a Jonatán y le preguntó: «¿Qué he hecho? ¿De qué delito soy culpable? ¿Qué mal le he hecho a tu padre? ¿Por qué quiere matarme?».

fr.L: Et David s’enfuit de Nayoth, à Rama, et il vint dire devant Jonathan : « Qu’ai-je fait ? Quelle [est] ma faute, et quel [est] mon péché devant ton père, pour qu’il cherche ma vie ? »
fr.B: David s’échappa de Nayoth, à Rama, et alla trouver Jonathan. « Qu’ai-je fait ? demanda-t-il. Quel est mon crime ? Quel tort ai-je fait à ton père, pour qu’il veuille m’ôter la vie ? »
fr.R: David s’est enfui de Nayoth, à Rama. Il est allé voir Jonathan et lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que j’ai fait ? De quel crime suis-je coupable ? Quel mal ai-je fait à ton père ? Pourquoi est-ce qu’il cherche à me tuer ? »

sw.L: Daudi akakimbia kutoka Nayothi katika Rama, akaja, akasema mbele ya Yonathani, "Nimefanya nini? Uovu wangu [ni] nini, na dhambi yangu [ni] nini mbele ya baba yako, hata anaitafuta nafsi yangu?"
sw.B: Daudi akatoroka kutoka Nayothi katika Rama, akaenda kwa Yonathani. Akauliza, "Nimefanya nini? Kosa langu ni lipi? Nimemkosea baba yako nini, hata anatafuta kuniua?"
sw.R: Daudi akakimbia kutoka Nayothi katika Rama. Akaenda kwa Yonathani, akamwuliza, "Nimefanya nini? Nina hatia ya kosa gani? Nimemkosea baba yako nini? Kwa nini anataka kuniua?"

vi.L: Đa-vít chạy trốn khỏi Na-giốt ở Ra-ma, đến và nói trước mặt Giô-na-than: "Em đã làm gì? Tội ác của em [là] gì, và tội lỗi của em trước mặt cha anh [là] gì, mà người tìm hại mạng sống em?"
vi.B: Đa-vít trốn khỏi Na-giốt thuộc Ra-ma và đến gặp Giô-na-than. Ông hỏi: "Em đã làm gì? Em mắc tội gì? Em đã làm điều sai trái nào với cha anh mà người tìm cách lấy mạng em?"
vi.R: Đa-vít chạy trốn khỏi Na-giốt thuộc Ra-ma. Ông đến gặp Giô-na-than và hỏi: "Em đã làm gì? Em có tội gì? Em đã làm gì sai với cha anh? Tại sao người tìm cách giết em?"

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 라마 나욧에서 도망쳐 와서 요나단 앞에서 말했다. "제가 무엇을 했어요? 제 죄악이 무엇이고, 당신의 아버지 앞에서 제 죄가 무엇이기에 그분이 제 목숨을 찾으세요?"
ko.B: 다윗은 라마 나욧에서 도망쳐 요나단에게 가서 물었다. "제가 무슨 일을 했어요? 제 죄가 무엇이에요? 제가 당신의 아버지께 무슨 잘못을 했기에, 그분이 제 목숨을 노리시는 거예요?"
ko.R: 다윗은 라마의 나욧에서 도망쳐 요나단에게 가서 물었다. "제가 무엇을 했어요? 제가 무슨 죄를 지었어요? 당신의 아버지께 무슨 잘못을 했어요? 왜 그분이 저를 죽이려고 하세요?"

decisions.choice: fled from Naioth in Ramah: David leaves Samuel's refuge
decisions.reason: David had fled to Samuel at Naioth in Ramah, and Saul's messengers and then Saul himself, coming to seize him, were overcome by the Spirit and prophesied (19:18-24). David uses the delay to escape. Naioth may mean "dwellings" or "camps"; it seems to name a place in or near Ramah where Samuel's prophets lived.

decisions.choice: iniquity and sin: any wrongdoing that would deserve punishment
decisions.reason: David uses two common words for wrongdoing, guilt and sin, to say that he has done nothing at all against Saul. He asks the same three questions that Jonathan will put to Saul in verse 32.

decisions.choice: seeking my life: trying to kill me
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is a set way of saying that someone is out to kill them (22:23; 23:15; Exodus 4:19).

decisions.choice: crime; wrong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the two terms for wrongdoing; Literal keeps "iniquity" and "sin".

decisions.choice: tú between David and Jonathan
alternatives: usted from David to the king's son
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets: one person is always tú; David's respect for Jonathan shows in “tu siervo” (verses 7-8), not in a formal pronoun.

decisions.choice: David speaks to Jonathan in the polite informal style (해요체) with "당신"; Jonathan answers in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for this pair after their covenant (18:3): close friends, with David still giving the king's son the respect of the polite ending.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֣וֹ חָלִילָה֮ לֹ֣א תָמוּת֒ הִנֵּ֡ה לֹֽא־יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה אָבִ֜י דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל א֚וֹ דָּבָ֣ר קָטֹ֔ן וְלֹ֥א יִגְלֶ֖ה אֶת־אָזְנִ֑י וּמַדּוּעַ֩ יַסְתִּ֨יר אָבִ֥י מִמֶּ֛נִּי אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֵ֥ין זֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Far be it! Not you will die. Look, not does my father a thing great or a thing small and not he uncovers my ear. And why would hide my father from me this thing? Not [is] this.

en.L: And he said to him, "Far from it! You will not die. Look, my father does not do anything great or anything small without uncovering my ear. And why would my father hide this thing from me? It [is] not so."
en.B: Jonathan answered, "Never! You are not going to die. My father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. Why would he hide this from me? It is not so."
en.R: "No!" Jonathan said. "You will not die! My father does not do anything, big or small, without telling me first. Why would he keep this a secret from me? It cannot be true."

es.L: Y él le dijo: «¡De ninguna manera! No morirás. He aquí que mi padre no hace cosa grande ni cosa pequeña sin descubrir mi oído. ¿Y por qué me ocultaría mi padre esta cosa? No [es] así».
es.B: Jonatán le respondió: «¡Jamás! No vas a morir. Mi padre no hace nada, grande ni pequeño, sin decírmelo. ¿Por qué me iba a ocultar esto? No es así».
es.R: «¡No!», le dijo Jonatán. «¡No vas a morir! Mi padre no hace nada, grande o pequeño, sin decírmelo primero. ¿Por qué me iba a guardar esto en secreto? No puede ser verdad».

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Loin de là ! Tu ne mourras pas. Voici, mon père ne fait aucune chose, grande ou petite, sans m’en découvrir l’oreille. Et pourquoi mon père me cacherait-il cette chose ? Il n’en [est] rien. »
fr.B: Jonathan lui répondit : « Jamais de la vie ! Tu ne mourras pas. Mon père ne fait rien, ni grand ni petit, sans me le dire. Pourquoi me cacherait-il cela ? Ce n’est pas possible. »
fr.R: « Non ! a dit Jonathan. Tu ne vas pas mourir ! Mon père ne fait rien, rien de grand ni de petit, sans me le dire d’abord. Pourquoi est-ce qu’il me cacherait cela ? Ce n’est pas vrai. »

sw.L: Akamwambia, "Hasha! Hutakufa. Tazama, baba yangu hafanyi jambo lolote kubwa wala jambo lolote dogo bila kunifunulia sikio. Basi kwa nini baba yangu anifiche jambo hili? Sivyo."
sw.B: Yonathani akajibu, "Hasha! Hutakufa. Baba yangu hafanyi jambo lolote, liwe kubwa au dogo, bila kuniambia. Kwa nini anifiche jambo hili? Sivyo hivyo."
sw.R: Yonathani akasema, "Hapana! Hutakufa! Baba yangu hafanyi jambo lolote, kubwa au dogo, bila kuniambia kwanza. Kwa nini anifiche jambo hili? Haiwezekani kuwa kweli."

vi.L: Giô-na-than nói với ông: "Không đời nào! Em sẽ không chết. Kìa, cha anh không làm việc gì, lớn hay nhỏ, mà không mở tai cho anh. Vậy tại sao cha anh lại giấu anh việc này? Không [phải] vậy đâu."
vi.B: Giô-na-than đáp: "Không bao giờ! Em sẽ không chết đâu. Cha anh không làm việc gì, dù lớn hay nhỏ, mà không cho anh biết. Tại sao cha lại giấu anh việc này? Không phải vậy đâu."
vi.R: Giô-na-than nói: "Không! Em sẽ không chết đâu! Cha anh không làm việc gì, lớn hay nhỏ, mà không nói cho anh biết trước. Tại sao cha lại giấu anh chuyện này? Không thể có chuyện đó được."

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그에게 말했다. "절대로 그렇지 않다! 너는 죽지 않을 것이다. 보아라, 내 아버지께서는 큰일이든 작은 일이든 내 귀를 열어 주지 않고는 하시지 않는다. 그런데 내 아버지께서 어찌 이 일을 나에게 숨기시겠느냐? 그렇지 않다."
ko.B: 요나단이 대답했다. "절대로 그럴 리 없다! 너는 죽지 않는다. 내 아버지께서는 큰일이든 작은 일이든 나에게 알리지 않고는 아무것도 하지 않으신다. 그런데 어찌 이 일만 나에게 숨기시겠느냐? 그럴 리가 없다."
ko.R: 요나단이 말했다. "아니다! 너는 죽지 않을 거다! 내 아버지께서는 큰일이든 작은 일이든 나에게 먼저 말씀하지 않고는 아무 일도 하지 않으신다. 그런데 왜 이 일만 나에게 비밀로 하시겠느냐? 그럴 리가 없다."

decisions.choice: far be it: a strong denial
decisions.reason: The word means something like "unthinkable!" and is used to push away an idea as wrong or impossible (verse 9; 14:45; Genesis 18:25).

decisions.choice: uncover my ear: tell me, let me know
decisions.reason: Uncovering someone's ear was a picture for telling them something in confidence (9:15; 20:12-13; 22:8). Jonathan says his father keeps nothing from him.

decisions.choice: does not do: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: At this point the consonants written in the Hebrew text and the reading the scribes noted in the margin differ slightly in the form of the verb ("has done" or "does"). The text follows the margin. Either way, Jonathan says that his father tells him everything he plans.

decisions.choice: it is not so: Jonathan rejects David's fear
decisions.reason: The two short words at the end mean "This is not [the case]." Jonathan sincerely believes his father has given up the plan, as Saul had sworn (19:6).

decisions.choice: telling me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture "uncovering my ear"; Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע ע֜וֹד דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יָדֹ֨עַ יָדַ֜ע אָבִ֗יךָ כִּֽי־מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אַל־יֵֽדַע־זֹ֥את יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן פֶּן־יֵֽעָצֵ֑ב וְאוּלָ֗ם חַי־יְהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ כִּ֣י כְפֶ֔שַׂע בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הַמָּֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And swore again David and said, Surely knows your father that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, Let not know this Jonathan, lest he be grieved. But truly, [as] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, but like a step [is] between me and death.

en.L: But David swore again and said, "Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, 'Do not let Jonathan know this, or he will be grieved.' But truly, [as] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, [there is] but about a step between me and death."
en.B: But David answered him with an oath: "Your father knows very well that you think well of me, and he has said to himself, 'Jonathan must not know this, or it will grieve him.' But as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, there is only a step between me and death."
en.R: But David made a solemn promise. He said, "Your father knows very well that you are my friend. So he has said to himself, 'Jonathan must not find out about this. It would upset him.' But I tell you, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I am only one step away from death."

es.L: Pero David volvió a jurar y dijo: «Tu padre sabe bien que he hallado gracia ante tus ojos, y ha dicho: “Que no sepa esto Jonatán, no sea que se entristezca”. Pero ciertamente, vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y vive tu alma, que apenas [hay] un paso entre mí y la muerte».
es.B: Pero David le respondió con un juramento: «Tu padre sabe muy bien que tú me aprecias, y se ha dicho: “Jonatán no debe saber esto, porque le dolería”. Pero tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y que tú vives, estoy a un paso de la muerte».
es.R: Pero David le hizo una promesa solemne: «Tu padre sabe muy bien que eres mi amigo. Por eso se ha dicho: “Jonatán no debe enterarse de esto. Le dolería”. Pero te digo, tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y que tú vives, que estoy a un solo paso de la muerte».

fr.L: Mais David jura encore et dit : « Ton père sait bien que j’ai trouvé grâce à tes yeux, et il s’est dit : “Que Jonathan ne le sache pas, de peur qu’il ne s’afflige.” Mais vraiment, [aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et [que] ton âme est vivante, il n’y a qu’un pas entre moi et la mort. »
fr.B: Mais David lui répondit par un serment : « Ton père sait très bien que tu as de l’amitié pour moi, et il s’est dit : “Il ne faut pas que Jonathan le sache, cela lui ferait de la peine.” Pourtant, aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, il n’y a qu’un pas entre moi et la mort. »
fr.R: Mais David lui a fait une promesse solennelle. Il a dit : « Ton père sait très bien que tu es mon ami. Alors il s’est dit : “Jonathan ne doit pas l’apprendre. Cela lui ferait de la peine.” Mais je te le dis, aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je suis à un pas de la mort. »

sw.L: Lakini Daudi akaapa tena, akasema, "Baba yako anajua hakika kwamba nimepata kibali machoni pako, naye amesema, 'Yonathani asijue jambo hili, asije akahuzunika.' Lakini kwa kweli, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama nafsi yako iishivyo, [iko] kama hatua moja tu kati yangu na kifo."
sw.B: Lakini Daudi akamjibu kwa kiapo, "Baba yako anajua vizuri kwamba wewe unanipenda, naye amejisemea, 'Yonathani asijue jambo hili, lisije likamhuzunisha.' Lakini kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama uishivyo, imebaki hatua moja tu kati yangu na kifo."
sw.R: Lakini Daudi akaapa kwa kiapo kizito. Akasema, "Baba yako anajua vizuri kwamba wewe ni rafiki yangu. Kwa hiyo amejisemea, 'Yonathani asijue jambo hili. Lingemhuzunisha.' Lakini ninakuambia, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama uishivyo, nimebakiza hatua moja tu kufa."

vi.L: Nhưng Đa-vít lại thề và nói: "Cha anh biết rõ rằng em được ơn trước mắt anh, nên người đã nói: 'Đừng để Giô-na-than biết việc này, kẻo nó buồn rầu.' Nhưng thật, thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như linh hồn anh đang sống, giữa em và cái chết chỉ còn khoảng một bước chân."
vi.B: Nhưng Đa-vít lại thề: "Cha anh biết rất rõ là anh quý mến em, nên người tự nhủ: 'Không được để Giô-na-than biết việc này, kẻo nó buồn lòng.' Nhưng thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như anh đang sống, giữa em và cái chết chỉ còn một bước."
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít thề. Ông nói: "Cha anh biết rất rõ anh là bạn của em. Vì vậy người tự nhủ: 'Không được để Giô-na-than biết chuyện này. Nó sẽ buồn lắm.' Nhưng em nói thật với anh, thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như anh đang sống, em chỉ còn cách cái chết một bước chân thôi."

ko.L: 그러나 다윗이 다시 맹세하며 말했다. "당신의 아버지는 제가 당신의 눈에 은총을 얻은 줄을 잘 아시고, '요나단이 이것을 알지 못하게 하자. 그가 슬퍼할 것이다' 하고 말씀하셨어요. 그러나 진실로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 당신의 목숨을 두고 맹세하는데, 저와 죽음 사이는 겨우 한 걸음뿐이에요."
ko.B: 그러나 다윗은 맹세하며 대답했다. "당신의 아버지는 당신이 저를 아끼는 줄을 잘 알고 계세요. 그래서 '요나단이 이 일을 알면 마음 아파할 테니 알리지 말아야겠다' 하고 생각하셨을 거예요. 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 당신의 목숨을 두고 맹세하는데, 저는 죽음에서 겨우 한 걸음 떨어져 있어요."
ko.R: 그러나 다윗은 엄숙하게 맹세하며 말했다. "당신의 아버지는 당신이 제 친구라는 것을 잘 아세요. 그래서 '요나단이 이 일을 알면 속상해할 테니 알게 하지 말자' 하고 생각하셨을 거예요. 하지만 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 당신의 목숨을 두고 맹세하는데, 저는 죽음에서 딱 한 걸음 떨어져 있어요."

decisions.choice: swore again: answered with an oath
decisions.reason: David meets Jonathan's denial with an oath of his own. "Again" may mean that he swore a second time, or simply that he replied, now under oath, to what Jonathan had said.

decisions.choice: found favor in your eyes: you think well of me
decisions.reason: The phrase means that someone looks on another with kindness and goodwill (verse 29; 16:22). Saul knows how close his son is to David (18:1-4; 19:1-7).

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives: a double oath
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath (14:39, 45; 19:6). David adds Jonathan's own life to it. "Your soul" here means simply "you" in person.

decisions.choice: about a step between me and death: I am close to being killed
decisions.reason: The picture is of a man who could fall into death with one step. Saul's spear had already missed David twice (18:11; 19:10).

decisions.choice: he has said to himself
decisions.reason: The verb "say" often means "think" or "say to oneself" (verse 26). David is guessing at Saul's reasoning, not reporting a speech.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד מַה־תֹּאמַ֥ר נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said Jonathan to David, Whatever says your soul, and I will do for you.

en.L: And Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul says, I will do for you."
en.B: Jonathan said to David, "Whatever you want, I will do for you."
en.R: Jonathan told David, "I will do anything you want me to do."

es.L: Y dijo Jonatán a David: «Lo que diga tu alma, eso haré por ti».
es.B: Jonatán le dijo a David: «Lo que tú quieras, eso haré por ti».
es.R: Jonatán le dijo a David: «Haré todo lo que quieras que haga».

fr.L: Et Jonathan dit à David : « Ce que dira ton âme, je le ferai pour toi. »
fr.B: Jonathan dit à David : « Tout ce que tu voudras, je le ferai pour toi. »
fr.R: Jonathan a dit à David : « Je ferai tout ce que tu voudras. »

sw.L: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Lolote isemalo nafsi yako, nitakufanyia."
sw.B: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Lolote utakalo, nitakufanyia."
sw.R: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Nitafanya lolote unalotaka nikufanyie."

vi.L: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Linh hồn em nói điều gì, anh sẽ làm cho em điều ấy."
vi.B: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Em muốn gì, anh cũng sẽ làm cho em."
vi.R: Giô-na-than bảo Đa-vít: "Em muốn anh làm gì, anh cũng sẽ làm."

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "네 영혼이 말하는 것은 무엇이든지 내가 너를 위해 하겠다."
ko.B: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "네가 바라는 것은 무엇이든 해 주겠다."
ko.R: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "네가 원하는 것은 무엇이든지 다 해 주겠다."

decisions.choice: whatever your soul says: whatever you wish
decisions.reason: "Soul" here is the person's own desire (Deuteronomy 14:26). Jonathan places himself at David's disposal, as his covenant friend (18:3).

decisions.choice: whatever you want
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom; Literal keeps "your soul says".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן הִֽנֵּה־חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ מָחָ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֛י יָשֹׁב־אֵשֵׁ֥ב עִם־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וְשִׁלַּחְתַּ֨נִי֙ וְנִסְתַּרְתִּ֣י בַשָּׂדֶ֔ה עַ֖ד הָעֶ֥רֶב הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Jonathan, Look, [the] new moon [is] tomorrow, and I surely should sit with the king to eat; and you will send me away, and I will hide in the field until the evening, the third.

en.L: And David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow [is the] new moon, and I ought to sit with the king to eat. But let me go, and I will hide myself in the field until the third evening.
en.B: David said to Jonathan, "Listen, tomorrow is the new moon festival, and I am expected to sit at the table with the king. But let me go, and I will hide in the field until the evening of the third day.
en.R: David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow is the new moon festival. I am supposed to eat with the king. But let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the day after tomorrow.

es.L: Y dijo David a Jonatán: «He aquí que mañana [es] luna nueva, y yo debería sentarme con el rey a comer. Pero déjame ir, y me esconderé en el campo hasta la tarde del tercer [día].
es.B: David le dijo a Jonatán: «Mira, mañana es la fiesta de la luna nueva, y se espera que yo me siente a la mesa con el rey. Pero déjame ir, y me esconderé en el campo hasta la tarde del tercer día.
es.R: David le dijo a Jonatán: «Mira, mañana es la fiesta de la luna nueva. Yo debo comer con el rey. Pero déjame ir a esconderme en el campo hasta la tarde de pasado mañana.

fr.L: Et David dit à Jonathan : « Voici, demain [c’est la] nouvelle lune, et moi, je devrais m’asseoir avec le roi pour manger. Mais laisse-moi partir, et je me cacherai dans la campagne jusqu’au soir du troisième [jour].
fr.B: David dit à Jonathan : « Écoute, demain, c’est la fête de la nouvelle lune, et je dois normalement prendre place à table avec le roi. Mais laisse-moi partir, et je me cacherai dans la campagne jusqu’au soir du troisième jour.
fr.R: David a dit à Jonathan : « Écoute, demain, c’est la fête de la nouvelle lune. Je dois manger avec le roi. Mais laisse-moi partir. Je vais me cacher dans la campagne jusqu’au soir d’après-demain.

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Yonathani, "Tazama, kesho [ni] mwandamo wa mwezi, nami sina budi kuketi pamoja na mfalme kula. Lakini niache niende, nami nitajificha shambani mpaka jioni ya [siku ya] tatu.
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Yonathani, "Sikiliza, kesho ni sikukuu ya mwezi mpya, nami natazamiwa kuketi mezani pamoja na mfalme. Lakini niache niende, nami nitajificha shambani mpaka jioni ya siku ya tatu.
sw.R: Daudi akamwambia Yonathani, "Tazama, kesho ni sikukuu ya mwezi mpya. Natakiwa kula pamoja na mfalme. Lakini niache niende nikajifiche shambani mpaka jioni ya kesho kutwa.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Giô-na-than: "Kìa, ngày mai [là] ngày trăng mới, và em phải ngồi ăn với vua. Nhưng xin anh để em đi, và em sẽ trốn ngoài đồng cho đến chiều ngày thứ ba.
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với Giô-na-than: "Anh xem, mai là lễ trăng mới, và em phải ngồi dự tiệc với vua. Nhưng xin anh để em đi, em sẽ trốn ngoài đồng cho đến chiều ngày thứ ba.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với Giô-na-than: "Anh xem, mai là lễ trăng mới. Em phải ăn tiệc với vua. Nhưng xin anh để em đi trốn ngoài đồng cho đến chiều ngày mốt.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 요나단에게 말했다. "보세요, 내일은 초하루예요. 저는 왕과 함께 앉아 먹어야 해요. 그러나 저를 보내 주세요. 제가 사흘째 저녁까지 들에 숨어 있을게요.
ko.B: 다윗이 요나단에게 말했다. "보세요, 내일은 초하루 축제예요. 저는 왕과 함께 식탁에 앉아야 해요. 그러나 저를 보내 주세요. 모레 저녁까지 들에 숨어 있을게요.
ko.R: 다윗이 요나단에게 말했다. "내일은 초하루 축제예요. 저는 왕과 함께 식사를 해야 해요. 하지만 저를 보내 주세요. 모레 저녁까지 들판에 숨어 있을게요.

decisions.choice: new moon: the feast at the start of the month
decisions.reason: The day of the new moon began each month. It was kept with offerings, trumpet blasts and a meal (Numbers 10:10; 28:11-15; 2 Kings 4:23). Here the king's household eats together for two days (verse 27), and David, as one of the king's own men, is expected to be there.

decisions.choice: I surely should sit: I am expected to sit
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses the obligation. David's absence will be noticed.

decisions.choice: until the third evening: until the evening of the day after tomorrow
alternatives: until the evening of the third day from tomorrow
decisions.reason: Counting today as the first day, the third day is the second day of the feast (verses 12, 19, 27, 34). David plans to stay hidden until Jonathan can bring word after both days.

decisions.choice: new moon festival
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "festival" so that the reader knows that the new moon was a feast day with a meal.

decisions.choice: la fiesta de la luna nueva
decisions.reason: The new moon was a feast at the start of the month (m1); Balanced and Readable name the feast, as the English “new moon festival” (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "mwandamo wa mwezi" (L); "sikukuu ya mwezi mpya" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal names the new moon itself; Balanced and Readable add that it was a feast, as the English adds "festival" (m1).

decisions.choice: "ngày trăng mới" (L); "lễ trăng mới" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The feast at the new moon, the start of the month (m1); Balanced and Readable name the festival as the English does.

decisions.choice: "초하루 축제" (new moon festival) at Balanced and Readable; "초하루" at Literal
decisions.reason: The feast at the start of the month (meaning decision m1); "월삭" is the older church word, "초하루" is plain Korean.

source.text: אִם־פָּקֹ֥ד יִפְקְדֵ֖נִי אָבִ֑יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ נִשְׁאֹל֩ נִשְׁאַ֨ל מִמֶּ֤נִּי דָוִד֙ לָרוּץ֙ בֵּֽית־לֶ֣חֶם עִיר֔וֹ כִּ֣י זֶ֧בַח הַיָּמִ֛ים שָׁ֖ם לְכָל־הַמִּשְׁפָּחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If surely misses me your father, and you will say, Asked urgently from me David to run [to] Bethlehem his city, for [the] sacrifice of the days [is] there for all the clan.

en.L: If your father misses me at all, then you will say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me to run [to] Bethlehem, his city, for the yearly sacrifice [is] there for the whole clan.'
en.B: If your father notices that I am missing, tell him, 'David begged me to let him hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because the whole clan is holding its yearly sacrifice there.'
en.R: If your father sees that I am not there, tell him, 'David asked me if he could hurry home to Bethlehem. His whole family is offering the yearly sacrifice there.'

es.L: Si tu padre me echa de menos, dirás: “David me pidió con insistencia que lo dejara ir corriendo [a] Belén, su ciudad, porque allí [hay] sacrificio anual para todo el clan”.
es.B: Si tu padre nota que falto, dile: “David me rogó que lo dejara ir de prisa a Belén, su pueblo, porque todo su clan celebra allí el sacrificio anual”.
es.R: Si tu padre ve que no estoy, dile: “David me pidió permiso para ir rápido a su casa en Belén. Toda su familia está ofreciendo allí el sacrificio anual”.

fr.L: Si ton père remarque vraiment mon absence, tu diras : “David m’a demandé avec insistance [la permission] de courir à Bethléem, sa ville, car il y a là le sacrifice annuel pour tout le clan.”
fr.B: Si ton père remarque mon absence, dis-lui : “David m’a supplié de le laisser aller en hâte à Bethléem, sa ville, parce que tout son clan y offre le sacrifice annuel.”
fr.R: Si ton père voit que je ne suis pas là, dis-lui : “David m’a demandé s’il pouvait aller vite chez lui, à Bethléem. Toute sa famille y offre le sacrifice de chaque année.”

sw.L: Ikiwa baba yako atanikosa kabisa, basi utasema, 'Daudi aliniomba sana ruhusa kukimbilia Bethlehemu, mji wake, kwa maana dhabihu ya kila mwaka [iko] huko kwa ajili ya ukoo wote.'
sw.B: Baba yako akiona kwamba sipo, mwambie, 'Daudi aliniomba sana nimruhusu aharakishe kwenda Bethlehemu, mji wake, kwa sababu ukoo wote unatoa dhabihu yake ya kila mwaka huko.'
sw.R: Baba yako akiona kwamba sipo, mwambie, 'Daudi aliniomba ruhusa ya kuharakisha kwenda nyumbani Bethlehemu. Jamaa yake yote inatoa dhabihu ya kila mwaka huko.'

vi.L: Nếu cha anh nhận ra em vắng mặt, thì anh hãy nói: 'Đa-vít đã nài xin em cho anh ấy chạy [về] Bết-lê-hem, thành của anh ấy, vì ở đó có lễ tế hằng năm cho cả gia tộc.'
vi.B: Nếu cha anh thấy em vắng mặt, anh hãy thưa: 'Đa-vít đã nài xin con cho anh ấy vội về Bết-lê-hem, quê nhà của anh ấy, vì cả gia tộc đang dâng sinh tế hằng năm ở đó.'
vi.R: Nếu cha anh thấy em không có mặt, anh hãy thưa: 'Đa-vít xin con cho anh ấy vội về nhà ở Bết-lê-hem. Cả gia đình anh ấy đang dâng sinh tế hằng năm ở đó.'

ko.L: 만일 당신의 아버지가 저를 찾으시면 '다윗이 자기 성읍 베들레헴으로 달려가게 해 달라고 나에게 간청했습니다. 그곳에서 온 집안이 해마다 드리는 제사가 있기 때문입니다' 하고 말씀하세요.
ko.B: 당신의 아버지께서 제가 없는 것을 아시면 이렇게 말씀드리세요. '다윗이 고향 베들레헴에 급히 다녀오게 해 달라고 간청했습니다. 그곳에서 온 집안이 해마다 드리는 제사가 있답니다.'
ko.R: 당신의 아버지께서 제가 없는 것을 보시면 이렇게 말씀드리세요. '다윗이 고향 베들레헴에 급히 다녀와도 되겠느냐고 저에게 물었습니다. 그의 온 집안이 그곳에서 해마다 드리는 제사를 드린답니다.'

decisions.choice: misses me: notices that I am absent
decisions.reason: The verb means to look for someone and find them missing. The same verb is used of David's empty seat in verses 18, 25 and 27.

decisions.choice: asked urgently: begged
decisions.reason: The doubled verb makes David's request sound pressing. Jonathan repeats it in verse 28.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of the days: the yearly family sacrifice
decisions.reason: "The days" here means a yearly cycle, as with Elkanah's yearly sacrifice (1:21; 2:19). Bethlehem was the town of David's family (16:1-5; 17:12).

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable uses "family" for the clan, the group of related households.

source.text: אִם־כֹּ֥ה יֹאמַ֛ר ט֖וֹב שָׁל֣וֹם לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְאִם־חָרֹ֤ה יֶֽחֱרֶה֙ ל֔וֹ דַּ֕ע כִּֽי־כָלְתָ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: If thus he says, Good, peace [is] to your servant; and if surely it burns to him, know that has been completed the evil from with him.

en.L: If he says thus, 'Good,' [there is] peace for your servant. But if he becomes very angry, know that harm has been determined by him.
en.B: Should he say, 'Good,' your servant is safe. But should he flare up in anger, you will know that he has made up his mind to do me harm.
en.R: If he says, 'All right,' then I am safe. But if he gets very angry, you can be sure that he has decided to hurt me.

es.L: Si dice así: “Bien”, [habrá] paz para tu siervo. Pero si se enoja mucho, sabe que el mal está decidido por él.
es.B: Si dice: “Está bien”, tu siervo estará a salvo. Pero si se enfurece, sabrás que ha decidido hacerme daño.
es.R: Si dice: “Está bien”, entonces estoy a salvo. Pero si se enoja mucho, puedes estar seguro de que ha decidido hacerme daño.

fr.L: S’il dit ainsi : “C’est bien”, [il y a] paix pour ton serviteur. Mais s’il s’enflamme de colère, sache que le malheur est décidé de sa part.
fr.B: S’il dit : “C’est bien”, ton serviteur n’a rien à craindre. Mais s’il s’emporte, tu sauras qu’il est résolu à me faire du mal.
fr.R: S’il dit : “D’accord”, alors je ne risque rien. Mais s’il se met très en colère, tu pourras être sûr qu’il a décidé de me faire du mal.

sw.L: Akisema hivi, 'Vyema,' [iko] amani kwa mtumishi wako. Lakini akikasirika sana, jua kwamba ubaya umekusudiwa naye.
sw.B: Akisema, 'Vyema,' mtumishi wako yuko salama. Lakini akiwaka hasira, utajua kwamba ameamua kunidhuru.
sw.R: Akisema, 'Sawa,' basi mimi niko salama. Lakini akikasirika sana, uwe na hakika kwamba ameamua kunidhuru.

vi.L: Nếu người nói thế này: 'Tốt,' thì đầy tớ của anh được bình an. Nhưng nếu người nổi giận, thì anh hãy biết rằng người đã quyết định làm hại [em].
vi.B: Nếu người nói: 'Được,' thì đầy tớ của anh được an toàn. Nhưng nếu người nổi giận, anh sẽ biết người đã quyết tâm hại em.
vi.R: Nếu người nói: 'Được,' thì em được an toàn. Nhưng nếu người nổi giận, anh có thể chắc chắn là người đã quyết định hại em.

ko.L: 그가 '좋다' 하고 말하면 당신의 종에게 평안이 있을 거예요. 그러나 그가 크게 화를 내면, 그에게서 해가 정해진 줄 아세요.
ko.B: 그분이 '좋다' 하시면 당신의 종은 무사할 거예요. 그러나 그분이 몹시 화를 내시면, 저를 해치기로 마음먹으신 줄 아세요.
ko.R: 그분이 '괜찮다' 하시면 저는 안전해요. 그러나 그분이 몹시 화를 내시면, 저를 해치기로 작정하신 줄 아세요.

decisions.choice: it surely burns to him: he flares up in anger
decisions.reason: Anger is spoken of as heat that burns (verse 30; 11:6). The doubled verb makes it strong.

decisions.choice: the evil has been completed: he has settled on harming me
decisions.reason: The verb means "to be finished" or "to be settled". The harm is decided and certain (verses 9 and 33; 25:17).

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "me"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was a common courtesy (Genesis 18:3). David uses it with the king's son, even though they are bound as friends.

decisions.choice: I; me
decisions.reason: Readable says "I" for the polite "your servant", which reads oddly in modern English.

decisions.choice: "mimi" (R); "mtumishi wako" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Between David and Jonathan, "your servant" is a courtesy (m3); Literal and Balanced keep "mtumishi wako", and Readable says "mimi", as the English Readable says "I". In speech to the king it stays "mtumishi wako" at every level.

decisions.choice: David's "your servant" to Jonathan: "đầy tớ của anh" (L, B), "em" (R)
decisions.reason: A polite way of saying "me" (m3); David keeps the formal words to the king's son at Literal and Balanced, as subjects do to the king, and Readable says "em".

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ חֶ֨סֶד֙ עַל־עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ כִּ֚י בִּבְרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הֵבֵ֥אתָ אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֖ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְאִם־יֶשׁ־בִּ֤י עָוֺן֙ הֲמִיתֵ֣נִי אַ֔תָּה וְעַד־אָבִ֖יךָ לָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה תְבִיאֵֽנִי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you will do chesed with your servant, for into [a] covenant of Yahweh you have brought your servant with you. And if there is in me iniquity, kill me you; and to your father why this you bring me?

en.L: So deal [in] steadfast love with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with you. But if there is iniquity in me, put me to death yourself. Why then should you bring me to your father?"
en.B: So show faithful love to your servant, because you brought your servant into a covenant with you before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But if I am guilty, kill me yourself. Why hand me over to your father?"
en.R: So show me faithful love, because you made a covenant with me before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But if I have done anything wrong, then kill me yourself! Why take me to your father?"

es.L: Haz, pues, amor leal con tu siervo, porque has hecho entrar a tu siervo contigo en un pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pero si hay en mí iniquidad, mátame tú; ¿por qué, pues, me has de llevar a tu padre?».
es.B: Muestra, pues, amor fiel a tu siervo, porque hiciste un pacto con tu siervo delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pero si soy culpable, mátame tú mismo. ¿Para qué entregarme a tu padre?».
es.R: Así que muéstrame amor fiel, porque hiciste un pacto conmigo delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pero si he hecho algo malo, ¡mátame tú mismo! ¿Para qué llevarme ante tu padre?».

fr.L: Agis donc avec amour loyal envers ton serviteur, car tu as fait entrer ton serviteur avec toi dans une alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Mais s’il y a de la faute en moi, fais-moi mourir toi-même. Pourquoi donc me mènerais-tu à ton père ? »
fr.B: Montre donc ton amour fidèle à ton serviteur, puisque tu as fait entrer ton serviteur dans une alliance avec toi devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mais si je suis coupable, tue-moi toi-même. Pourquoi me livrer à ton père ? »
fr.R: Alors montre-moi ton amour fidèle, puisque tu as fait une alliance avec moi devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mais si j’ai fait quelque chose de mal, alors tue-moi toi-même ! Pourquoi m’emmener chez ton père ? »

sw.L: Basi umtendee mtumishi wako upendo usiokoma, kwa maana umemwingiza mtumishi wako katika agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} pamoja nawe. Lakini ikiwa uovu umo ndani yangu, niue wewe mwenyewe. Kwa nini basi unipeleke kwa baba yako?"
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mtendee mtumishi wako fadhili, kwa sababu ulimwingiza mtumishi wako katika agano pamoja nawe mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Lakini kama nina hatia, niue wewe mwenyewe. Kwa nini unikabidhi kwa baba yako?"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nitendee fadhili, kwa sababu ulifanya agano nami mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Lakini kama nimekosa jambo lolote, niue wewe mwenyewe! Kwa nini unipeleke kwa baba yako?"

vi.L: Vậy xin anh đối xử với đầy tớ của anh bằng tình yêu thương thành tín, vì anh đã đem đầy tớ của anh vào một giao ước của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} với anh. Nhưng nếu trong em có tội ác, thì chính anh hãy giết em đi. Tại sao anh lại đem em đến cho cha anh?"
vi.B: Vậy xin anh tỏ lòng nhân từ với đầy tớ của anh, vì anh đã lập giao ước với đầy tớ của anh trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nhưng nếu em có tội, chính anh hãy giết em đi. Sao lại phải nộp em cho cha anh?"
vi.R: Vậy xin anh tỏ lòng nhân từ với em, vì anh đã lập giao ước với em trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nhưng nếu em đã làm điều gì sai, thì chính anh hãy giết em đi! Sao lại đem em nộp cho cha anh?"

ko.L: 그러니 당신의 종에게 한결같은 사랑을 베풀어 주세요. 당신이 당신의 종을 당신과 함께 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 언약 안으로 들어오게 했으니까요. 그러나 만일 제게 죄악이 있으면 당신이 직접 저를 죽이세요. 무엇 때문에 저를 당신의 아버지에게 데려가겠어요?"
ko.B: 그러니 당신의 종에게 인애를 베풀어 주세요. 당신은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 당신의 종과 언약을 맺었잖아요. 그러나 제게 죄가 있다면 당신이 직접 저를 죽이세요. 굳이 저를 당신의 아버지께 넘길 필요가 있겠어요?"
ko.R: 그러니 저에게 인애를 베풀어 주세요. 당신은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 저와 언약을 맺었잖아요. 하지만 제가 무슨 잘못을 했다면 차라리 당신이 저를 죽이세요! 왜 저를 당신의 아버지께 데려가려고 하세요?"

decisions.choice: chesed: loyal love that keeps faith with a bond
decisions.reason: Chesed is kindness that is owed and freely given within a relationship, here the covenant Jonathan made with David (18:3). It is the same word used of God's own love (Exodus 34:6) and of Ruth's loyalty (Ruth 1:8). David asks Jonathan to act on it.

decisions.choice: a covenant of Yahweh: the covenant of 18:3
decisions.reason: Jonathan had made a covenant with David because he loved him (18:3). It was made before Yahweh, who stands as its witness and guards it (verses 23, 42). David now calls it a covenant into which Jonathan himself "brought" him.

decisions.choice: kill me yourself: an emphatic "you"
decisions.reason: David adds the pronoun "you" for stress: if he is guilty, he would rather die at his friend's hand than be handed over to Saul.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is rendered the same way throughout, as in Exodus 34:6 and Ruth 1:8.

decisions.choice: Why hand me over to your father?
decisions.reason: "Why bring me to your father?" means "why let your father be the one to deal with me?"

decisions.choice: amour loyal (L); amour fidèle (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *ḥesed*, also between people: loyal love that keeps faith with a bond (m1); the same words in verses 14 and 15.

decisions.choice: amor leal (L); amor fiel (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *ḥesed*, also between people (m1, r-en-1): the loyal love that keeps faith with the covenant of 18:3. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "upendo usiokoma" (L); "fadhili" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note: *ḥesed* is "upendo usiokoma" at Literal and "fadhili" at Balanced and Readable, also between people bound by a covenant (m1).

decisions.choice: *ḥesed* between people: "tình yêu thương thành tín" (L); "lòng nhân từ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *ḥesed* between people; loyal love that keeps faith with a covenant (m1).

decisions.choice: *ḥesed* between David and Jonathan: "한결같은 사랑" (L); "인애" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The forms the terms of this translation set for 1 and 2 Samuel, also between people: the loyal love that keeps faith with a covenant bond (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "당신의 종" (your servant) to Jonathan at Literal and Balanced; "저" at Readable
decisions.reason: David speaks of himself humbly to the king's son, as the Hebrew does; Readable says "I", as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן חָלִ֣ילָה לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀אִם־יָדֹ֣עַ אֵדַ֗ע כִּֽי־כָלְתָ֨ה הָרָעָ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם אָבִי֙ לָב֣וֹא עָלֶ֔יךָ וְלֹ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Jonathan, Far be it from you! For if surely I knew that had been completed the evil from with my father to come upon you, then not it would I tell you?

en.L: And Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! For if I knew for certain that harm had been determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?"
en.B: Jonathan said, "Never think it! If I knew for certain that my father had decided to bring harm on you, would I not tell you?"
en.R: "Do not even think that!" Jonathan said. "If I found out that my father had decided to hurt you, of course I would tell you!"

es.L: Y dijo Jonatán: «¡Lejos esté eso de ti! Porque si yo supiera con certeza que mi padre ha decidido que el mal venga sobre ti, ¿no te lo diría?».
es.B: Jonatán le dijo: «¡Ni lo pienses! Si yo supiera con certeza que mi padre ha decidido hacerte daño, ¿no te lo diría?».
es.R: «¡Ni siquiera lo pienses!», le dijo Jonatán. «Si me enterara de que mi padre ha decidido hacerte daño, ¡claro que te lo diría!».

fr.L: Et Jonathan dit : « Loin de toi [cette pensée] ! Car si je savais avec certitude que mon père a décidé que le malheur vienne sur toi, ne te le dirais-je pas ? »
fr.B: Jonathan répondit : « N’y pense pas ! Si je savais avec certitude que mon père a décidé de te faire du mal, ne te le dirais-je pas ? »
fr.R: « N’y pense même pas ! a dit Jonathan. Si j’apprenais que mon père a décidé de te faire du mal, bien sûr que je te le dirais ! »

sw.L: Yonathani akasema, "Hasha kwako! Kwa maana kama ningejua hakika kwamba ubaya umekusudiwa na baba yako ukujie, je, nisingekuambia?"
sw.B: Yonathani akasema, "Usifikiri hivyo kamwe! Kama ningejua hakika kwamba baba yangu ameamua kukuletea madhara, je, nisingekuambia?"
sw.R: Yonathani akasema, "Usifikiri hivyo hata kidogo! Kama ningegundua kwamba baba yangu ameamua kukudhuru, hakika ningekuambia!"

vi.L: Giô-na-than nói: "Không đời nào có chuyện đó với em! Vì nếu anh biết chắc rằng cha anh đã quyết định đem tai họa đến trên em, chẳng lẽ anh không báo cho em sao?"
vi.B: Giô-na-than nói: "Đừng bao giờ nghĩ vậy! Nếu anh biết chắc cha anh đã quyết định hại em, lẽ nào anh lại không cho em biết?"
vi.R: Giô-na-than nói: "Đừng nghĩ thế! Nếu anh biết cha anh đã quyết định hại em, dĩ nhiên anh sẽ báo cho em!"

ko.L: 그러자 요나단이 말했다. "너는 그런 생각을 절대로 하지 마라! 내 아버지께서 너에게 해를 내리기로 정하신 것을 내가 확실히 알게 되면, 내가 어찌 너에게 알리지 않겠느냐?"
ko.B: 요나단이 말했다. "그런 생각은 하지도 마라! 내 아버지께서 너를 해치기로 마음먹으신 것을 내가 확실히 알게 되면, 내가 어찌 너에게 알리지 않겠느냐?"
ko.R: 요나단이 말했다. "그런 생각은 하지도 마라! 내 아버지께서 너를 해치기로 하신 것을 알게 되면, 당연히 너에게 말해 주겠다!"

decisions.choice: far be it from you: do not think such a thing
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. Here it rejects the thought that Jonathan could ever kill David or hand him over.

decisions.choice: would I not tell you?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The clause has no question word, but it reads most naturally as a question expecting the answer "Of course I would."

decisions.choice: of course I would tell you!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן מִ֖י יַגִּ֣יד לִ֑י א֛וֹ מַה־יַּעַנְךָ֥ אָבִ֖יךָ קָשָֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Jonathan, Who will tell me, or what [if] answers you your father harshly?

en.L: And David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me, or what if your father answers you harshly?"
en.B: David asked Jonathan, "Who will let me know if your father gives you a harsh answer?"
en.R: David asked Jonathan, "If your father answers you angrily, how will I find out?"

es.L: Y dijo David a Jonatán: «¿Quién me lo hará saber, o qué [pasa] si tu padre te responde con dureza?».
es.B: David le preguntó a Jonatán: «¿Quién me avisará si tu padre te responde con dureza?».
es.R: David le preguntó a Jonatán: «Si tu padre te responde enojado, ¿cómo me voy a enterar?».

fr.L: Et David dit à Jonathan : « Qui me [le] dira, ou quoi si ton père te répond durement ? »
fr.B: David demanda à Jonathan : « Qui me fera savoir si ton père te répond durement ? »
fr.R: David a demandé à Jonathan : « Si ton père te répond avec colère, comment est-ce que je le saurai ? »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Yonathani, "Ni nani atakayeniambia, au itakuwaje baba yako akikujibu kwa ukali?"
sw.B: Daudi akamwuliza Yonathani, "Ni nani atakayenijulisha kama baba yako atakujibu kwa ukali?"
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza Yonathani, "Baba yako akikujibu kwa hasira, nitajuaje?"

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Giô-na-than: "Ai sẽ báo cho em, hay [nếu] cha anh trả lời anh gay gắt thì sao?"
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi Giô-na-than: "Nếu cha anh trả lời anh gay gắt thì ai sẽ báo cho em biết?"
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi Giô-na-than: "Nếu cha anh trả lời anh một cách giận dữ, làm sao em biết được?"

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 요나단에게 말했다. "당신의 아버지가 당신에게 엄하게 대답하시면 누가 저에게 알려 주겠어요?"
ko.B: 다윗이 요나단에게 물었다. "당신의 아버지께서 당신에게 거칠게 대답하시면, 누가 저에게 알려 주지요?"
ko.R: 다윗이 요나단에게 물었다. "당신의 아버지께서 화를 내며 대답하시면, 제가 그걸 어떻게 알 수 있지요?"

decisions.choice: who will tell me, or what: who will tell me if
decisions.reason: The two questions belong together: David cannot come near Saul's table, so he asks how word will reach him if Saul answers harshly. Jonathan answers this in verses 12-23.

decisions.choice: who will let me know if
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two questions into one, which says the same thing more plainly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד לְכָ֖ה וְנֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיֵּצְא֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Jonathan to David, Come, and let us go out [to] the field. And went out the two of them [to] the field.

en.L: And Jonathan said to David, "Come, and let us go out [to] the field." And the two of them went out [to] the field.
en.B: Jonathan said to David, "Come, let us go out into the field." So the two of them went out together.
en.R: Jonathan said to David, "Come on, let us go out into the field." So they both went out there.

es.L: Y dijo Jonatán a David: «Ven, y salgamos [al] campo». Y salieron los dos [al] campo.
es.B: Jonatán le dijo a David: «Ven, salgamos al campo». Y los dos salieron juntos.
es.R: Jonatán le dijo a David: «Ven, vamos al campo». Así que los dos salieron allá.

fr.L: Et Jonathan dit à David : « Viens, et sortons dans la campagne. » Et ils sortirent tous deux dans la campagne.
fr.B: Jonathan dit à David : « Viens, sortons dans la campagne. » Et ils sortirent tous les deux.
fr.R: Jonathan a dit à David : « Viens, sortons dans la campagne. » Alors ils y sont allés tous les deux.

sw.L: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Njoo, twende shambani." Wawili hao wakatoka, [wakaenda] shambani.
sw.B: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Njoo, twende shambani." Basi wote wawili wakatoka pamoja.
sw.R: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Haya, twende shambani." Basi wote wawili wakatoka, wakaenda huko.

vi.L: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Hãy đến, chúng ta cùng ra đồng." Và hai người cùng ra đồng.
vi.B: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Nào, chúng ta ra ngoài đồng đi." Vậy hai người cùng đi ra.
vi.R: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Nào, mình ra ngoài đồng đi." Vậy cả hai cùng đi ra đó.

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "자, 들로 나가자." 그리고 그 둘이 들로 나갔다.
ko.B: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "자, 들로 나가자." 그래서 두 사람은 함께 들로 나갔다.
ko.R: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "자, 들판으로 나가자." 그래서 둘은 함께 들판으로 나갔다.

decisions.choice: the field: the open country outside the town
decisions.reason: "The field" is the land outside the town walls, used for crops and pasture. There the two could talk without being overheard, and Jonathan could show David the place for the signal (verses 19-22).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־אֶחְקֹ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֗י כָּעֵ֤ת׀מָחָר֙ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔ית וְהִנֵּה־ט֖וֹב אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וְלֹֽא־אָז֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֖יתִי אֶת־אָזְנֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jonathan to David, Yahweh, God of Israel! When I sound out my father about [this] time tomorrow, the third [day], and look, [it is] good toward David, then not will I send to you and uncover your ear?

en.L: And Jonathan said to David, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] God of Israel, [be witness]! When I sound out my father about this time tomorrow, [or] the third [day], and look, [he is] good toward David, will I not then send to you and uncover your ear?
en.B: Then Jonathan said to David, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, is my witness! By this time tomorrow, or the day after, I will sound out my father. If he is well disposed toward David, I will certainly send word and let you know.
en.R: Jonathan said to David, "I promise this before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. By this time tomorrow or the next day, I will find out what my father is thinking. If he feels good about you, I will send someone to tell you.

es.L: Y dijo Jonatán a David: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, [sea testigo]! Cuando yo sondee a mi padre mañana a esta hora, [o] al tercer [día], y he aquí [que está] bien con David, ¿no enviaré entonces a ti y descubriré tu oído?
es.B: Luego Jonatán le dijo a David: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, es mi testigo! Mañana a esta hora, o pasado mañana, sondearé a mi padre. Si está bien dispuesto hacia David, sin falta te mandaré aviso y te lo haré saber.
es.R: Jonatán le dijo a David: «Te prometo esto delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: mañana a esta hora o pasado mañana averiguaré lo que piensa mi padre. Si tiene buena disposición hacia ti, te mandaré a alguien para avisarte.

fr.L: Et Jonathan dit à David : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, [en est témoin] ! Quand je sonderai mon père vers cette heure-ci demain, [ou] le troisième [jour], et voici, [s’il est] bien disposé envers David, alors ne t’enverrai-je pas [quelqu’un] pour te découvrir l’oreille ?
fr.B: Puis Jonathan dit à David : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, m’en est témoin ! Demain à cette heure-ci, ou après-demain, je sonderai mon père. S’il est bien disposé envers David, je ne manquerai pas de t’envoyer quelqu’un pour te le faire savoir.
fr.R: Jonathan a dit à David : « Je te le promets devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël. Demain à cette heure-ci, ou après-demain, je vais découvrir ce que mon père pense. S’il est bien disposé envers toi, j’enverrai quelqu’un pour te le dire.

sw.L: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, [ni shahidi]! Nitakapomchunguza baba yangu karibu wakati huu kesho, [au siku ya] tatu, na tazama, [yu] mwema kwa Daudi, je, sitatuma kwako wakati huo na kukufunulia sikio?
sw.B: Kisha Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, ni shahidi wangu! Kesho wakati kama huu, au kesho kutwa, nitamchunguza baba yangu. Akiwa na nia njema kwa Daudi, hakika nitatuma ujumbe nikujulishe.
sw.R: Yonathani akamwambia Daudi, "Ninaahidi jambo hili mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli. Kesho wakati kama huu, au kesho kutwa, nitajua baba yangu anafikiri nini. Akiwa na nia njema kwako, nitatuma mtu akuambie.

vi.L: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "[Có] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên [chứng giám]! Khi anh dò ý cha anh vào giờ này ngày mai, [hay] ngày thứ ba, nếu kìa, [người] có ý tốt với Đa-vít, chẳng lẽ anh lại không sai người đến mở tai cho em sao?
vi.B: Rồi Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Có {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, làm chứng cho anh! Giờ này ngày mai hay ngày mốt, anh sẽ dò ý cha anh. Nếu người có thiện ý với Đa-vít, chắc chắn anh sẽ sai người báo cho em biết.
vi.R: Giô-na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Anh hứa điều này trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Giờ này ngày mai hay ngày mốt, anh sẽ tìm hiểu xem cha anh nghĩ gì. Nếu người có ý tốt với em, anh sẽ sai người đến báo cho em.

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 [증인이 되신다]! 내가 내일이나 모레 이맘때에 내 아버지의 뜻을 살펴보아, 보라, 다윗에게 좋으면, 그때 내가 너에게 사람을 보내어 네 귀를 열어 주지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 증인이시다! 내일이나 모레 이맘때에 내가 아버지의 마음을 떠보겠다. 아버지께서 다윗에게 좋은 마음을 품고 계시면, 내가 반드시 사람을 보내어 너에게 알려 주겠다.
ko.R: 요나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 약속한다. 내일이나 모레 이맘때까지 내가 아버지의 생각을 알아보겠다. 아버지께서 너를 좋게 여기고 계시면, 사람을 보내서 너에게 알려 주겠다.

decisions.choice: Yahweh, God of Israel!: the opening of an oath
alternatives: Yahweh, God of Israel, is witness
decisions.reason: Jonathan begins by naming Yahweh, but the sentence does not say what Yahweh is to be. The sense is an appeal to Yahweh as witness to the promise that follows (compare verses 23 and 42). Some ancient translations add the word "witness".

decisions.choice: this time tomorrow, the third day: by tomorrow or the day after
decisions.reason: Jonathan will test Saul's mood over the two days of the feast: tomorrow, and the third day counting from today (verses 5, 19, 27).

decisions.choice: uncover your ear: tell you
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: good toward David: well disposed to him
decisions.reason: "Good" here means that Saul is favorable, with no harm in mind (compare verse 7).

decisions.choice: is my witness; I promise this before
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the words that make the oath clear in English. Literal brackets them.

source.text: כֹּֽה־יַעֲשֶׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה לִֽיהוֹנָתָ֜ן וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֗יף כִּֽי־יֵיטִ֨ב אֶל־אָבִ֤י אֶת־הָֽרָעָה֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־אָזְנֶ֔ךָ וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֖יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וִיהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus may do Yahweh to Jonathan and thus may he add, if it pleases my father [to bring] the evil upon you, and I will uncover your ear and send you away, and you will go in peace. And may be Yahweh with you as he was with my father.

en.L: Thus may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do to Jonathan, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if my father is pleased [to bring] harm on you and I [do not] uncover your ear and send you away, so that you go in peace. And may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with my father.
en.B: But if my father means to do you harm, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} deal with me, Jonathan, ever so severely if I do not let you know and send you away to go in safety. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been with my father.
en.R: But if my father wants to hurt you, I will tell you and send you away safely. If I do not, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} punish me terribly. And may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with my father.

es.L: Así haga {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Jonatán, y aun añada, si a mi padre le parece bien [traer] el mal sobre ti y yo [no] descubro tu oído y te dejo ir para que te vayas en paz. Y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté contigo como estuvo con mi padre.
es.B: Pero si mi padre se propone hacerte daño, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me castigue a mí, Jonatán, y aun más, si no te lo hago saber y te dejo ir a salvo. Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté contigo como ha estado con mi padre.
es.R: Pero si mi padre quiere hacerte daño, te lo diré y te dejaré ir a salvo. Si no lo hago, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me castigue duramente. Y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté contigo, como estuvo con mi padre.

fr.L: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} traite ainsi Jonathan, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y ajoute encore, s’il plaît à mon père [d’amener] le malheur sur toi et que je ne te découvre pas l’oreille et ne te laisse pas partir pour que tu t’en ailles en paix. Et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit avec toi comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été avec mon père.
fr.B: Mais si mon père a l’intention de te faire du mal, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me traite, moi Jonathan, avec sévérité et plus encore, si je ne te le fais pas savoir et ne te laisse pas partir en sécurité. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit avec toi comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été avec mon père.
fr.R: Mais si mon père veut te faire du mal, je te le dirai et je te laisserai partir en sécurité. Sinon, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me punisse sévèrement. Et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit avec toi comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été avec mon père.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amtendee Yonathani hivyo, na kuzidi, ikiwa baba yangu atapenda [kukuletea] ubaya, nami [nisi]kufunulie sikio na kukuacha uende, upate kwenda kwa amani. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nawe kama alivyokuwa pamoja na baba yangu.
sw.B: Lakini baba yangu akikusudia kukudhuru, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anitendee mimi Yonathani hivyo, na kuzidi, nisipokujulisha na kukuacha uende salama. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awe pamoja nawe kama alivyokuwa pamoja na baba yangu.
sw.R: Lakini baba yangu akitaka kukudhuru, nitakuambia na kukuacha uende salama. Nisipofanya hivyo, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aniadhibu vikali. Tena {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nawe, kama alivyokuwa pamoja na baba yangu.

vi.L: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phạt Giô-na-than như vậy, và còn thêm nữa, nếu cha anh muốn [đem] tai họa đến trên em mà anh [không] mở tai cho em và để em đi, cho em đi bình an. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với em như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ở với cha anh.
vi.B: Nhưng nếu cha anh có ý hại em, mà anh không báo cho em biết và để em đi được an toàn, thì nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phạt Giô-na-than này thật nặng nề. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với em như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ở với cha anh.
vi.R: Nhưng nếu cha anh muốn hại em, anh sẽ báo cho em và để em đi an toàn. Nếu anh không làm vậy, nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phạt anh thật nặng. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với em như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ở với cha anh.

ko.L: 만일 내 아버지께서 너에게 해를 [내리기를] 좋게 여기시는데도, 내가 네 귀를 열어 주어 너를 보내 평안히 가게 하지 [않으면], {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 요나단에게 벌을 내리시고 더 내리셔도 좋다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 아버지와 함께 계셨던 것처럼 너와 함께 계시기를 바란다.
ko.B: 그러나 내 아버지께서 너를 해치려고 하시는데도 내가 너에게 알려서 무사히 떠나보내지 않는다면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 요나단에게 벌을 내리시고 더 내리셔도 좋다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 아버지와 함께 계셨던 것처럼 너와도 함께 계시기를 빈다.
ko.R: 그러나 내 아버지께서 너를 해치려고 하시면, 내가 너에게 알려서 무사히 떠나보내겠다. 그렇게 하지 않으면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 무서운 벌을 내리셔도 좋다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내 아버지와 함께 계셨던 것처럼 너와도 함께 계시기를 바란다.

decisions.choice: so may Yahweh do to Jonathan, and so may he add: a curse on oneself
decisions.reason: This is the form of a solemn oath: the speaker calls down punishment on himself if he fails to keep his word (3:17; 14:44; Ruth 1:17). The punishment is left unnamed. Jonathan speaks of himself by name.

decisions.choice: if my father intends harm and I do not tell you: what the oath binds Jonathan to
alternatives: if my father intends harm, I will tell you and send you away
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed. Its sense is that Jonathan puts himself under the curse if, when he learns that Saul means harm, he fails to warn David and send him safely away. The word "not" is not written but is implied by the oath form.

decisions.choice: as he was with my father: Yahweh's presence that once marked Saul
decisions.reason: Yahweh had been with Saul at the start of his reign (10:7), but his Spirit had left Saul and now Yahweh is with David (16:13-14; 18:12, 14, 28). Jonathan's wish quietly accepts that David is the one Yahweh has chosen.

decisions.choice: may the LORD deal with me, Jonathan
decisions.reason: Jonathan names himself in the third person; Balanced keeps the name but makes clear that he is the speaker.

decisions.choice: I will tell you ... If I do not, may the LORD punish me
decisions.reason: Readable puts the promise first and the curse after it, so that the oath is easy to follow.

decisions.choice: Que le SEIGNEUR traite ainsi Jonathan, et qu'il y ajoute encore (L); ... me traite avec sévérité et plus encore (B)
alternatives: Que le SEIGNEUR me fasse ceci et pire encore
decisions.reason: The self-curse of the oath (m1) in the form the Samuel terms note sets ("me traite avec sévérité et plus encore"); Literal keeps the Hebrew "thus ... and thus may he add" and Jonathan's name in the third person.

decisions.choice: Así haga el SEÑOR ... y aun añada (L); que el SEÑOR me castigue ... y aun más (B); que el SEÑOR me castigue duramente (R)
alternatives: Que Dios me castigue, y aun más
decisions.reason: A curse on oneself to seal an oath (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew form; Balanced uses the Samuel terms note's wording, with the divine name here as the Hebrew has it; Readable puts it plainly after the promise, as the English does (r-en-2). Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "BWANA amtendee Yonathani hivyo, na kuzidi"
decisions.reason: The self-curse of the oath follows the terms note's wording ("Mungu anitendee hivyo, na kuzidi"), with Jonathan naming himself as the Hebrew does (m1); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "Nguyện CHÚA phạt ... như vậy, và còn thêm nữa" (L); "thật nặng nề" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note gives "phạt ... nặng nề" for this oath; Literal keeps the Hebrew's "so may he do and so may he add".

decisions.choice: "주께서 이 요나단에게 벌을 내리시고 더 내리셔도 좋다" for the self-curse "Thus may the LORD do to Jonathan and more"
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set for this oath (meaning decision m1); Korean puts the condition first, since a sentence ends with its main verb; Readable says it in plain words.

source.text: וְלֹ֖א אִם־עוֹדֶ֣נִּי חָ֑י וְלֹֽא־תַעֲשֶׂ֧ה עִמָּדִ֛י חֶ֥סֶד יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א אָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And not if still I [am] alive, and not you will do with me [the] chesed of Yahweh, and not I will die?

en.L: And if I [am] still alive, will you not show me the steadfast love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that I do not die?
en.B: And if I am still alive then, will you not show me the faithful love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that I do not die?
en.R: If I am still alive then, please show me the faithful love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that I am not killed.

es.L: Y si todavía [estoy] vivo, ¿no me mostrarás el amor leal {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que no muera?
es.B: Y si todavía estoy vivo entonces, ¿no me mostrarás el amor fiel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que yo no muera?
es.R: Si todavía estoy vivo entonces, por favor, muéstrame el amor fiel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que no me maten.

fr.L: Et si je [suis] encore vivant, ne me montreras-tu pas l’amour loyal {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, afin que je ne meure pas ?
fr.B: Et si je suis encore en vie à ce moment-là, ne me montreras-tu pas l’amour fidèle {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, afin que je ne meure pas ?
fr.R: Si je suis encore vivant à ce moment-là, je t’en prie, montre-moi l’amour fidèle {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, pour que je ne sois pas tué.

sw.L: Na ikiwa mimi [ni] bado hai, je, hutanitendea upendo usiokoma wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nisife?
sw.B: Na kama bado nitakuwa hai wakati huo, je, hutanitendea fadhili za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nisife?
sw.R: Kama bado nitakuwa hai wakati huo, tafadhali nitendee fadhili za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ili nisiuawe.

vi.L: Nếu anh còn sống, chẳng phải em sẽ tỏ cho anh tình yêu thương thành tín của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, để anh không chết sao?
vi.B: Nếu lúc ấy anh vẫn còn sống, em há không tỏ cho anh lòng nhân từ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, để anh khỏi chết sao?
vi.R: Nếu lúc ấy anh vẫn còn sống, xin em tỏ cho anh lòng nhân từ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, để anh không bị giết.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 아직 살아 있다면, 너는 나에게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 한결같은 사랑을 베풀어 내가 죽지 않게 하지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 그리고 그때 내가 아직 살아 있다면, 너는 나에게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 인애를 베풀어 내가 죽지 않게 해 주지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 그때 내가 아직 살아 있다면, 부디 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 베푸시는 것 같은 인애를 나에게 베풀어서 내가 죽임을 당하지 않게 해 다오.

decisions.choice: the three "nots": a plea in the form of a question
alternatives: O that, while I am still alive, you would show me the chesed of Yahweh
If I am still alive, you will not show me ... and I will not die (statements)
decisions.reason: The verse repeats "not" three times, and its grammar is hard. It is read here as a question that expects "yes": "If I am alive, will you not show me ... so that I do not die?" The first word could also be read with different vowels as "O that", giving a wish: "O that, while I am still alive, you would show me ...". The plea is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the chesed of Yahweh: loyal love such as Yahweh shows
decisions.reason: Chesed is loyal love within a bond (verse 8). "Of Yahweh" may mean love like Yahweh's own, or love that was pledged before Yahweh and that he will hold the parties to. Both point to faithfulness beyond what is usual.

decisions.choice: so that I do not die: Jonathan foresees a change of king
decisions.reason: When a new family took the throne, the old king's family was often put to death (1 Kings 15:29; 16:11; 2 Kings 10:11). Jonathan asks David, the future king, to spare him and his family.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: please show me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the request it implies.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־תַכְרִ֧ת אֶֽת־חַסְדְּךָ֛ מֵעִ֥ם בֵּיתִ֖י עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וְלֹ֗א בְּהַכְרִ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־אֹיְבֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not you will cut off your chesed from with my house forever, and not when cuts off Yahweh the enemies of David, each from upon [the] face of the ground.

en.L: And do not cut off your steadfast love from my house forever, not even when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cuts off the enemies of David, each one from the face of the ground."
en.B: And never cut off your faithful love from my family, not even when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cut off David's enemies, every one of them, from the face of the earth."
en.R: And never stop showing faithful love to my family, not even when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has wiped out every one of your enemies from the earth."

es.L: Y no cortes tu amor leal de mi casa para siempre, ni aun cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} corte a los enemigos de David, a cada uno de sobre la faz de la tierra».
es.B: Y nunca dejes de mostrar tu amor fiel a mi familia, ni siquiera cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haya eliminado de la faz de la tierra a todos los enemigos de David».
es.R: Y nunca dejes de mostrar amor fiel a mi familia, ni siquiera cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haya acabado con todos tus enemigos en la tierra».

fr.L: Et ne retranche jamais ton amour loyal de ma maison, pas même quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} retranchera les ennemis de David, chacun de la surface du sol. »
fr.B: Ne retire jamais ton amour fidèle à ma famille, pas même quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aura retranché de la surface de la terre tous les ennemis de David, jusqu’au dernier. »
fr.R: Et n’arrête jamais de montrer ton amour fidèle à ma famille, même quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aura fait disparaître de la terre tous tes ennemis, jusqu’au dernier. »

sw.L: Wala usiukatilie mbali upendo wako usiokoma na nyumba yangu milele, hata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakapowakatilia mbali adui za Daudi, kila mmoja wao, kutoka katika uso wa nchi."
sw.B: Kamwe usiikatilie mbali jamaa yangu fadhili zako, hata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakapokuwa amewakatilia mbali adui wote wa Daudi, kila mmoja wao, kutoka katika uso wa dunia."
sw.R: Kamwe usiache kuitendea jamaa yangu fadhili, hata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakapokuwa amewaangamiza adui zako wote duniani."

decisions.choice: cut off ... cuts off: a play on one verb
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: David must not "cut off" his love from Jonathan's family when Yahweh "cuts off" David's enemies. The verb is also the one used for "making" a covenant (verse 16; 18:3). Jonathan asks that David's victory, which he expects, should not sweep away his own family.

decisions.choice: my house: my family and descendants
decisions.reason: "House" means the household and the line that comes after it.

decisions.choice: forever: kept after Jonathan's death
decisions.reason: David remembered this oath when he was king. He sought out Jonathan's son Mephibosheth to show him chesed for Jonathan's sake (2 Samuel 9:1, 7) and spared him later (2 Samuel 21:7).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: your enemies
decisions.reason: Jonathan speaks of "David's enemies" while speaking to David. Readable says "your enemies" so the reader does not wonder who is meant.

decisions.choice: retrancher ... retranchera
decisions.reason: The same verb twice (m1); Literal keeps one French verb for both so that the play is heard.

decisions.choice: no cortes ... cuando el SEÑOR corte
alternatives: no quites ... cuando el SEÑOR elimine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one verb, “cut off” (m1); Literal keeps the same Spanish verb twice, the other levels use the plain words.

decisions.choice: "kukatilia mbali ... kuwakatilia mbali"
decisions.reason: Swahili can keep the one verb used twice (m1): David must not "cut off" his love when the LORD "cuts off" his enemies.

decisions.choice: "끊다" (cut off) for both uses of the verb
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one verb, Jonathan's plea and Yahweh's judgment (meaning decision m1); Korean "끊다" can carry both and keeps the echo at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן עִם־בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וּבִקֵּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִיַּ֖ד אֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

en.B: So Jonathan made a covenant with David's house, and said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} call David's enemies to account."
en.R: So Jonathan made a covenant with David's family. He said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} punish David's enemies."

es.L: Así cortó Jonatán [un pacto] con la casa de David, [diciendo]: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [lo] demande de la mano de los enemigos de David».
es.B: Así Jonatán hizo un pacto con la casa de David, y dijo: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pida cuentas a los enemigos de David».
es.R: Así Jonatán hizo un pacto con la familia de David. Dijo: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} castigue a los enemigos de David».

fr.L: Et Jonathan conclut [une alliance] avec la maison de David, [en disant] : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [en] demande compte à la main des ennemis de David ! »

fr.R: Ainsi, Jonathan a fait une alliance avec la famille de David. Il a dit : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} punisse les ennemis de David ! »

sw.L: Yonathani akakata [agano] na nyumba ya Daudi, [akisema], "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na alitake [hilo] mkononi mwa adui za Daudi."
sw.B: Basi Yonathani akafanya agano na nyumba ya Daudi, akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awadai adui za Daudi hesabu."
sw.R: Basi Yonathani akafanya agano na jamaa ya Daudi. Akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awaadhibu adui za Daudi."

vi.L: Vậy Giô-na-than kết [giao ước] với nhà Đa-vít, [nói rằng]: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đòi [nợ ấy] nơi tay các kẻ thù của Đa-vít."

vi.R: Vậy Giô-na-than lập giao ước với gia đình Đa-vít. Ông nói: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trừng phạt các kẻ thù của Đa-vít."

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 다윗의 집과 [언약을] 맺으며 [말했다]. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗의 원수들의 손에서 [그것을] 찾으시기를 바란다."
ko.B: 이렇게 요나단은 다윗의 집안과 언약을 맺고 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗의 원수들에게 책임을 물으시기를 바란다."
ko.R: 이렇게 요나단은 다윗의 집안과 언약을 맺었다. 요나단이 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗의 원수들을 벌하시기를 바란다."

decisions.choice: cut: made a covenant
decisions.reason: "Cut" is short for "cut a covenant", the usual way of saying "make a covenant" (11:1-2; 18:3; 22:8). The word "covenant" is left out, as it sometimes is.

decisions.choice: require from the hand of: call to account, punish
decisions.reason: To "require" something from someone's hand is to hold them responsible for it (Genesis 9:5; Ezekiel 3:18). The covenant now binds the two families, Jonathan's and David's.

decisions.choice: the words of the oath: Jonathan's curse, perhaps softened
alternatives: and Yahweh required it at the hand of David's enemies (narration)
may Yahweh call David to account (if he breaks it)
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish spoken by Jonathan, as here, or as the narrator's statement that Yahweh did call David's enemies to account. In curses, scribes sometimes wrote "David's enemies" in place of "David" to avoid putting a curse on him (25:22). If so, the sense is that Yahweh will hold David himself to account if he breaks the covenant.

decisions.choice: saying
decisions.reason: English supplies "saying" to show that the wish is Jonathan's words. Literal brackets it.

fr.R: Jonathan a demandé à David de refaire sa promesse, parce qu’il l’aimait. Il aimait David autant qu’il s’aimait lui-même.

vi.B: Giô-na-than lại bảo Đa-vít thề vì tình thương mình dành cho ông, vì Giô-na-than yêu ông như yêu chính mình.

ko.B: 요나단은 다윗을 사랑했으므로, 그 사랑을 두고 다윗에게 다시 맹세하게 했다. 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신처럼 사랑했다.
ko.R: 요나단은 다윗에게 한 번 더 약속해 달라고 했다. 요나단이 다윗을 사랑했기 때문이다. 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신만큼 사랑했다.

decisions.choice: he loved him as his own soul: the love of 18:1-3
decisions.reason: The same words describe how Jonathan first loved David after he killed Goliath (18:1, 3). "His soul" means his own self, his life.

decisions.choice: Jonathan made David swear again
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has Jonathan making David repeat his oath. An ancient Greek translation reads "Jonathan swore again to David". In both, the two friends bind themselves once more.

decisions.choice: by his love for him: the ground of the oath
decisions.reason: The oath rests on Jonathan's love for David. It may be that Jonathan appeals to that love as the reason for the oath, or that David swears by the love between them.

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 그에게 말했다. "내일은 초하루다. 네 자리가 비어 있을 것이니 네가 없는 것이 드러날 것이다.

decisions.choice: missed ... empty: one verb used twice
decisions.reason: The same verb, which means "to look for and find missing", is used of David being missed and of his seat being empty (verses 6, 25, 27).

decisions.choice: People will notice that you are not there
decisions.reason: Readable names who will miss David and puts the passive verb in active form.

ko.L: 그리고 사흘째 되는 날에 너는 빨리 내려가서, 그 일이 있던 날에 네가 숨었던 곳으로 가서, 에셀 바위 곁에 머물러 있어라.

decisions.choice: do it on the third day, go down quickly
decisions.reason: The first verb is formed from the number three and seems to mean "do on the third day" (verses 5 and 12). "Greatly" with "go down" may mean "quickly" or "far down". Both fit a man hurrying to his hiding place.

decisions.choice: the day of the deed: probably when Saul first plotted against David
decisions.reason: This seems to point back to the day when Jonathan told David to hide in the field while he spoke to his father (19:1-3). The phrase is short and its reference is not certain.

decisions.choice: the stone Ezel: a landmark whose name is uncertain
decisions.reason: Ezel appears only here, and the name may mean "departure". An ancient Greek translation reads "beside that mound", and has the same word in verse 41 where the Hebrew has "the south". The place was a landmark in the field near which David could hide.

decisions.choice: when this trouble began; when all this trouble began
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the short phrase "the day of the deed" most likely refers to; see m2.

decisions.choice: "에셀 바위" for the stone Ezel
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean form of the name; the meaning of the name is uncertain (meaning decision m3), so it is kept as a name.

en.R: I will shoot three arrows near the stone, as if I were practicing at a target.

es.L: Y yo tiraré tres flechas a su lado, como si [las] lanzara a un blanco.
